name: How does a curbless shower compare to a traditional walk-in shower with a curb?

mainEntity.name: How does a curbless shower compare to a traditional walk-in shower with a curb?

acceptedAnswer.text: While both eliminate tubs, curbless showers offer zero-threshold entry flush with the floor, whereas standard walk-in showers have a 3- to 5-inch raised curb. Standard curbed showers cost less to install because they do not require structural joist modification or recessed subfloors; the curb acts as a dam to contain standing water. However, curbless designs provide seamless transitions ideal for aging in place, wheelchair access, and a continuous visual flow across tile floors. Choosing between them involves balancing budget constraints against long-term accessibility goals and modern design preferences.
acceptedAnswer.description: Curbless showers sit flush with the bathroom floor for zero-barrier entry, whereas traditional walk-in showers feature a raised 3- to 5-inch dam to contain water.
